name: Temperature
description: Cold Sweat gives you a body temperature.

pages.title: Temperature
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Too hot or too cold and you take damage and cannot sleep
- Spawn can be snowy: **insulate early**
- Dress for the biome and the season, and keep a heat source nearby
- Higher is colder

Cold Sweat gives you a body temperature. Hot or cold places push it up or down, and if it goes too far you take damage and cannot sleep.\
\
It is a layer of survival, not a puzzle: dress for the biome and keep a heat source nearby.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** spawn can be snowy. Without warm gear you will freeze once the 5 minute [#](7A3C9A)[grace period](entry://glossary/grace)[#]() ends, so [#](2E5AAC)[insulate](entry://survival/temperature_gear)[#]() early.

pages.title: Thermometer
pages.text: Shows the temperature of the place you stand in. Your body temperature has its own icon on the HUD.

pages.title: Two numbers
pages.text:
**World temperature** is what the spot feels like: biome, season, time of day, height or depth, nearby fire, lava or ice, water.\
\
**Body temperature** drifts toward it. Armor insulation and warm or cold blocks slow that drift.

pages.title: Seasons
pages.text:
The [#](2E5AAC)[season](entry://survival/seasons)[#]() moves every biome's temperature: Mid Summer adds the most heat, Mid Winter takes the most away.\
\
In a temperate forest a summer noon is about 100 °F and a winter night about 40 °F, both just outside the comfortable 45 to 100 °F.

pages.title: Cold nights
pages.text:
Nights are the coldest part of the day. Bare-skinned on a temperate beach in Mid Winter you start freezing after a few minutes.\
\
One lit campfire within a few blocks keeps you warm there. Snowy biomes and peaks still need [#](2E5AAC)[warm clothes](entry://survival/temperature_gear)[#]() or a Hearth.
Leather or fur armor slows the drift enough to get through it; iron armor does not. See [#](2E5AAC)[Insulation and Heaters](entry://survival/temperature_gear)[#]().

pages.title: Water and danger
pages.text: Getting wet cools you, and a netherite diving suit makes you immune to that. Rain only soaks you so far, even after a swim; under a roof you dry off, faster where it's warm. Heat and cold can both be lethal.

pages.title: Caves and roofs
pages.text:
Underground, weather and season stop mattering: about 20 blocks down it is near 60 °F all year, a bit warmer deeper, unless lava is near.\
\
A roof overhead evens out heat and cold a little, so a cave or house is a good place to wait out a winter night. The Aether is mild too.

pages.title: Sleep and Grace
pages.text:
You cannot sleep while overheating or freezing.\
\
After you spawn or die you get Grace, a short immunity to temperature damage.

pages.title: Altitude
pages.text:
Higher is colder. The pack adds [#](2E5AAC)[Cold Sweat: Altitude](entry://survival/temperature_create)[#](), which splits the height range into bands that change temperature, adds a chill message in the sky and lets shelter or a sewn Windproof Lining cut the effect.\
\
Mountains, sky islands and airships are where it bites.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** Cold Sweat is gentler here: body temperature moves at 0.6 speed, you are comfortable down to about 45 °F instead of 50 °F, winter and the cold ends of spring and autumn are half as cold, and each hit does half a heart every 2 seconds instead of a full heart.

pages.title: Space
pages.text: Cold Sweat covers the Overworld and Aether. Northstar's planets have their own temperature system, set by each world and a Temperature Regulator block. It is separate from Cold Sweat, with one link: space suits count as warm clothing, so a suit keeps you warm on a cold night back home. The Martian Steel suit keeps out heat too.

pages.title: Related
pages.text:
